types.name: CutMotion
types.doc: How the tool moves during one cut, in the workpiece frame.

fields.name: Path
fields.doc: The tool tip follows `geometry` with the tool axis along +Z throughout.

types.name: CutMove
types.doc: One tool motion through the stock, with where it came from.

fields.name: rapid
fields.doc: Rapid moves should not touch stock; cutting them is a diagnostic.

fields.name: opIndex
fields.doc: Index of the source operation in the program's op list.

types.name: CutMoves
types.doc: Builds stock moves from a controller-independent toolpath.

fields.name: fromProgram
fields.doc:
Tool-tip moves in the workpiece frame: each programmed point is placed by
its setup's work origin, the active G43 length and the loaded tool's own
length (see `ToolpathFrame`), less the optional stock origin. Moves made
before any tool change are skipped: there is no tool in the spindle to
simulate.

types.name: CutReport
types.doc: What one `Stock.cut` call did, move by move.

fields.name: removed
fields.doc: Volume each move removed, in the order given.

fields.name: rapidContacts
fields.doc: Rapid moves that removed more than `tolerance` of material (cubic metres).

fields.name: collisions
fields.doc: Moves whose shank or holder overlapped more than `tolerance` of stock (cubic metres).

fields.name: byOperation
fields.doc: Totals per source operation, in order of first appearance.

types.name: MoveOutcome
types.doc:
What one move did to the stock, in cubic metres: the material its flutes
removed, and the stock left after that cut which its shank and holder
overlapped. Contact is measured after the move's own cut, so a climbing
move whose shank meets material its flutes remove later is not reported.

fields.name: source
fields.doc: Index of the move in the stock's history.

types.name: OperationTotals
types.doc: Removal and contact summed over the moves of one source operation.

types.name: RingComparison
types.doc:
Per-circle angular errors (radians), axial-major, radial index fastest.
Arc lengths and cell-volume estimates use mm and cubic mm. This is geometric
leftover/gouge, not an ISO gear grade; HB4 supplies metrology evaluation.

types.name: RingCut
types.doc:
Remove one counterclockwise angular span on a radial circle and consecutive Z cells.
start wraps; sweep is in [0,2*pi]. Gash/pass identifiers must be non-negative.

fields.name: new
fields.signature: (radialIndex:Int, axialFirst:Int, axialCount:Int, start:Float, sweep:Float, gash:Int, pass:Int):Void

types.name: RingGearTarget
types.doc:
Samples an ideal, undeformed spur gear on an existing ring lattice.
Only angular crossings are solved; there is no angular tessellation error.

types.name: RingGrid
types.doc:
Cell-centred circumferential grid. Millimetres; angles about +Z from +X.
Bounds are exact; cell sizes divide the bounds and never exceed requested spacing.

fields.name: sectorVolume
fields.doc: Volume of a one-radian sector of a cell, in cubic mm.

types.name: RingInterval
types.doc:
Sorted material arc [lo,hi] in [0,2*pi]. Artificial seam boundaries are not surfaces.
Each real exposed endpoint retains its gash and pass; -1 means original stock.

types.name: RingPreviewWorker
types.doc: Single-flight, bounded snapshot preview. Worker owns its contour stock and only transfers buffers.

types.name: RingSnapshot
types.doc: Immutable copy-on-write radial layers. Survives destruction of the original stock.

types.name: RingStock
types.doc:
Circumferential stock for gear cutting. Millimetres, radians; unlike Cartesian Stock's metres.
Exact angular interval endpoints at cell-centred (r,z) samples. No angle raster.

fields.name: fromGearBlank
fields.doc:
Cylindrical tooth band plus a continuous wall. wallThickness is measured BELOW
the external tooth roots (outside internal roots), not from the blank's tip circle.

fields.name: cutRegion
fields.doc: Entire batch is validated before native mutation; array order determines overlapping sources.

fields.name: cutSlab
fields.doc: Exact analytic intersection with a transverse planar slab, through the full Z range.

fields.name: compare
fields.doc: Geometric comparison against the complete GearKit tooth, root and tip fillets included.

fields.name: contour
fields.doc:
Boundary of the piecewise-cell solid. Angular chords only affect display.
Streams use mm; convert to metres when passing to the existing app scene.

types.name: Stock
types.doc:
In-process stock on a `StockLattice`, held by StockKit core: a grid of rays
along Z, and along X and Y too when the lattice is tri-dexel. Each ray keeps
sorted material intervals whose ends record the outward normal and the move
that made them. Every cut updates every grid; volumes, per-move removal and
contact, tiles and previews use the Z grid.

Only the cutting zone of each tool removes material; its shank and holder
are swept too, and their overlap with the stock is reported per move. Moves
cut in order; every cut move is kept in `history` and its index there is
the source recorded on the surfaces it made.

fields.name: ORIGINAL
fields.doc: Source of surfaces no move has touched.

fields.name: grid
fields.doc: The Z grid.

fields.name: empty
fields.doc: Stock with no material, to build up with `add`.

fields.name: box
fields.signature: (lattice:StockLattice, minX:Float, minY:Float, minZ:Float, maxX:Float, maxY:Float, maxZ:Float):Stock
fields.doc: A solid box; rays on its sides count as inside.

fields.name: fromTriangles
fields.doc:
Stock from a closed triangle mesh with outward, counter-clockwise faces:
`positions` holds xyz triples and `indices` vertex triples. A ray through
a shared edge or vertex is counted exactly once.

fields.name: fromMesh
fields.doc: Stock from a CadKit tessellation (vertex and index buffers in native layout).

fields.name: setThreads
fields.doc:
Threads the core cuts with: 0 (the default) means one per hardware
thread. The result is bit-identical for any count.

fields.name: cut
fields.doc:
Removes the material each move's flutes sweep, in order, and measures
the stock each move's shank and holder overlap after its cut.

fields.name: add
fields.doc:
Adds the material each move's cutting zone sweeps, in order: the stock becomes its union with it, from empty
stock if need be. The surfaces a move makes face out of what it swept and record its index in `history` as
their source. Returns the volume each move added (cubic metres, measured on the Z grid). A bead of filament is
such a move: the tool is the bead's cross-section revolved about the nozzle's axis.

fields.name: compare
compareAll
fields.doc:
The stock compared with `target` along every grid of its lattice, X, Y
then Z (only Z unless tri-dexel). Walls gouged sideways show on the X
and Y grids; each grid estimates the same volumes on its own.

fields.name: snapshot
fields.doc:
Captures the stock and, unless `withHistory` is false, its history; see
`StockSnapshot`. The history costs a copy as long as it, so leave it out
where the moves are not needed, as for colouring by deviation.

fields.name: restore
fields.doc: Returns the stock and its history to `snapshot`, which must share its lattice.

fields.name: tilesX
fields.doc: Z-grid tiles across (x) and down (y); tile (tx, ty) holds rays from (tx, ty) times the tile size.

fields.name: tileRevisions
fields.doc: Each Z-grid tile's revision, row by row; it changes whenever the tile's rays change.

fields.name: mesh
fields.doc:
A column mesh of `tilesWide` by `tilesHigh` Z tiles from tile (tileX,
tileY): each Z ray drawn as a square column spacing wide with exact
depths. With `merge`, equal faces along rows are joined (not with
`rayColors`); `bottoms` closes the columns. Colours come from `rayColors`
(one 0xRRGGBBAA per ray of the Z grid) if given, else from `palette`
indexed by source with `original` for untouched stock.

fields.name: contour
fields.doc:
A closed surface over `tilesWide` by `tilesHigh` Z tiles from tile (tileX,
tileY), dual-contoured from all three grids: walls and floors at the
rays' exact crossings with their normals and sources, sharp edges and
corners kept, features thinner than a spacing possibly lost. Needs a
tri-dexel lattice. `BySource` colours each surface by its move (pass
`palette`, one colour per history entry, to reuse one already built);
`ByDeviation` colours each surface by the gouge or leftover its own ray
finds there against the target, so walls cut too deep show as well as
floors. Without `coloring` the mesh is white.

fields.name: ray
fields.doc: The intervals along ray (i, j) of the grid along `axis` (Z by default), in increasing order.

fields.name: rays
fields.doc: Intervals of every ray in a block of the grid along `axis` (Z by default), i fastest.

fields.name: volume
fields.doc: Material volume as the grid along `axis` (Z by default) measures it: interval lengths times spacing squared.

fields.name: intervalCount
fields.doc: Intervals over every grid.

fields.name: raysTested
fields.doc: Rays whose sweep the core evaluated over every cut so far.

fields.name: bytes
fields.doc: Bytes the core holds for this stock.

fields.name: sweep
fields.doc:
The material one move of `tool` would sweep along the ray through (u, v)
on `axis` (see `StockAxis`), for checking the core against references.
Uses the tool's cutting zone, as `cut` does.

types.name: StockAxis
types.doc:
The direction a ray runs along: Z rays pass through (x, y), X rays through
(y, z) and Y rays through (x, z).

types.name: StockColoring
types.doc: How a stock preview colours its surfaces. Colours are 0xRRGGBBAA.

fields.name: BySource
fields.doc: Surfaces take the colour of the move that made them; untouched stock takes `original`.

fields.name: ByDeviation
fields.doc:
Against a target stock on the same lattice: gouges deeper than
`tolerance` in `gouge`, leftover thicker than `tolerance` in `leftover`,
the rest in `onTarget`. Contoured meshes judge each surface by its own
ray (walls by X and Y rays, floors by Z rays); column meshes judge each
Z ray as a whole.

types.name: StockComparison
types.doc:
Stock compared with a target part ray by ray along one grid's rays.
Leftover is stock outside the target and gouge is target missing from the
stock, as lengths along each ray; volumes multiply by the ray spacing
squared. Z rays see floors and ceilings; X and Y rays see walls, so a wall
gouged sideways shows on them.

fields.name: leftover
fields.doc: Per ray, i fastest.

fields.name: gougeSource
fields.doc: Source (history index) of the move that cut the largest gouge on each ray, or -1.

fields.name: deepestGouge
fields.doc: Deepest single gouge along any ray.

fields.name: thickestLeftover
fields.doc: Thickest single stretch of leftover along any ray.

fields.name: gougingMoves
fields.doc: Sources of moves whose gouges exceed `tolerance` somewhere, each once, in increasing order.

types.name: StockComponent
types.doc:
One material component on the dexel lattice. Areas/volumes are sampled,
just as Stock.volume is; supportArea is material crossing supportPlaneZ.

fields.name: new
fields.signature: (seedRay:Int, seedZ:Float, supportArea:Float, volume:Float, min:Array<Float>, max:Array<Float>, samples:Int, regions:Array<Float>):Void

types.name: StockComponents
types.doc:
Four-neighbour XY connectivity, joining only intervals with positive Z
overlap. A thin onion skin connects a part; stacked layers and diagonal-only
contact do not. Streams two rows instead of materialising a sheet's rays.

fields.name: measure
fields.doc: Call at a completed cut checkpoint; the stock must not change mid-scan.

types.name: StockGrid
types.doc:
The rays of a `StockLattice` along one axis: ray (i, j) passes through
(u, v) = (originU + i * spacing, originV + j * spacing), where u and v are
the other two axes in order: (x, y) for Z rays, (y, z) for X rays and
(x, z) for Y rays. Units are metres.

types.name: StockInterval
types.doc:
Material along a ray between heights `lo` and `hi`. Each end keeps the
outward normal of the material there and the source of the move that made
it: an index into the stock's move history, or `Stock.ORIGINAL` for
surfaces no move has touched.

types.name: StockLattice
types.doc:
A lattice of nodes (originX + i * spacing, originY + j * spacing, originZ +
k * spacing) and a grid of rays through them along each of its axes:
Z rays through (x_i, y_j), X rays through (y_j, z_k) and Y rays through
(x_i, z_k). The Z grid is always present; `triDexel` adds X and Y, which
every cut then updates too. Units are metres.

fields.name: new
fields.signature: (originX:Float, originY:Float, originZ:Float, spacing:Float, countX:Int, countY:Int, countZ:Int, ?triDexel:Bool):Void

fields.name: covering
fields.signature: (minX:Float, minY:Float, minZ:Float, maxX:Float, maxY:Float, maxZ:Float, spacing:Float, ?triDexel:Bool):StockLattice
fields.doc:
Nodes at the centres of `spacing` cells covering the box with one cell
to spare on every side, so no ray lies in a face of the box and the
stock's outside is always sampled.

fields.name: grid
fields.doc: The rays along `axis`.

types.name: StockMesh
types.doc:
A display mesh of part of a stock, as byte streams ready for a renderer:
float xyz positions and normals per vertex, uint32 triangle indices, RGBA8
colours per vertex, and the source move of each triangle for picking: a
column mesh (`Stock.mesh`) or a contoured surface (`Stock.contour`).

fields.name: new
fields.signature: (vertexCount:Int, triangleCount:Int, positions:Bytes, normals:Bytes, indices:Bytes, colors:Bytes, triangleSources:Bytes):Void

fields.name: sourceAt
fields.doc: The source (history index) of the move that made `triangle`'s surface, or `Stock.ORIGINAL`.

types.name: StockPreview
types.doc:
Keeps display meshes of a stock in chunks of tiles and rebuilds only the
chunks whose tiles changed since the last `update`: contoured surfaces for
a tri-dexel stock, else columns. A chunk also depends on the tiles just
past its +x and +y edges, whose rays it reads. Headless: hand the meshes to
a renderer.

fields.name: chunkTiles
fields.doc: Tiles per chunk side.

fields.name: meshes
fields.doc: Current mesh of each chunk, row by row; null until the first update.

fields.name: update
fields.doc: Rebuilds changed chunks and returns their indices (chunk (cx, cy) is cy * chunksX + cx).

fields.name: pick
fields.doc:
The move that made the surface under a picked triangle of chunk `chunk`,
or null for untouched stock: the link from a click on the preview to the
operation and source line (`move.opIndex`, `move.provenance`).

types.name: StockPreviewUpdate
types.doc: The chunks one refresh rebuilt: chunk `chunks[k]` now has mesh `meshes[k]`.

types.name: StockPreviewWorker
types.doc:
A `StockPreview` contoured on a worker thread, so cutting never waits for
meshing. `refresh` hands the worker a snapshot of `source`, which costs a
pointer per tile since tiles are shared until the next cut changes them;
the worker restores it into a stock of its own, contours the chunks that
changed and posts their meshes, which `take` returns on the caller's
thread. Only the caller's thread touches `source`.

fields.name: refresh
fields.doc: Starts a refresh of what `source` is now, unless one is under way; returns whether it started.

fields.name: take
fields.doc: The refreshes finished since the last call, oldest first; throws the worker's failure.

fields.name: wait
fields.doc: Waits for the refresh under way, if any.

fields.name: dispose
fields.doc: Stops the worker and releases its stock. Returns once it has stopped.

types.name: StockSnapshot
types.doc:
A stock as it was, sharing tiles with it until either side changes them.
Restoring it also restores the move history it had.

fields.name: new
fields.doc: Made by `Stock.snapshot`.

types.name: StockTimeline
types.doc:
Scrubs through a program: the stock after any number of its moves. Cuts
the whole program once, keeping a snapshot every `interval` moves; seeking
restores the nearest snapshot at or before the position and cuts forward.

fields.name: position
fields.doc: Moves cut into the stock so far.

fields.name: outcomes
fields.doc: What each move did when the whole program was first cut, in program order.

fields.name: new
fields.doc: `stock` must be fresh (no history); it ends at the program's end.

fields.name: seek
fields.doc: Shows the stock after the first `target` moves.

types.name: FaceEndpointStock
types.doc:
Adds physically cut Z=0 and Z=faceWidth circles to an existing inspection.
Interior coordinates are unchanged. These planes are sampling domains, not
extra material or an extrapolation of unseen face ends.

types.name: GashPass
types.doc:
An exact master-phase crossing and its engagement window (seconds).
A window may straddle many controller ticks. center may lie outside the
requested run when an already engaged edge crosses a run boundary.

fields.name: constantSpeed
fields.doc: Constant-speed events come from integer phase indices, never tick accumulation.

fields.name: fromMotion
fields.doc: Exact phase crossings under piecewise-linear master interpolation.

types.name: HobbingAxes
types.doc:
mm/radians. X is the work/hob centre distance, Y shift along the hob axis,
Z the hob head height. A is signed tilt from -Y towards +Z. B and C are
right-hand, unwrapped spindle and table angles.

fields.name: poseValues
fields.doc:
Hob +X faces the work centre; hob +Z points along the tilted -Y axis.
The final inverse C rotation expresses the cut in the workpiece frame.

fields.name: nativePose
fields.doc: Materialize only accepted samples; midpoint error checks stay in Haxe.

types.name: HobbingErrorJob

fields.name: new
fields.signature: (spec:GearSpec, hob:HobDesign, at:(Float) -> HobbingAxes, passes:Array<GashPass>, sources:Array<HobbingErrorSource>, wall:Float, radialStep:Float, axialStep:Float, firstTooth:Int, lastTooth:Int, tolerance:Float, ?inspection:GearInspection, ?motionKnots:Array<Float>, ?threads:Int, ?inspectionCross:Bool, ?faceEndpoints:Bool, ?stockGrid:RingGrid):Void

types.name: HobbingErrorSource
types.doc:
Identified error with provenance. Perturbs tool/work motion before cutting,
never metrology values after the fact. Dimensions mm/rad/s; phases explicit.

fields.name: new
fields.signature: (id:String, part:String, basis:String, apply:(Float, HobbingAxes) -> HobbingAxes, ?warp:(Point3) -> Point3):Void

fields.name: tableTilt
fields.doc:
Load-induced tilt, separate from axial TIR. Force is machine-radial N;
bearing pivot depth/force height mm, moment stiffness Nm/rad.

fields.name: latency
fields.signature: (part:String, delay:Float, ratio:Float, master:(Float) -> Float, velocity:(Float) -> Float, predict:Bool):HobbingErrorSource
fields.doc:
Diagnostic latency model. A runtime study should instead supply the measured
C error in apply(), avoiding double counting encoder/servo errors already present.

fields.name: profile
fields.doc:
Assumed radial form waveform on a zero-rake hob's planar rake regions.
Does not claim a measured profile map or arbitrary-rake planarity.

types.name: HobbingForceHistory
types.doc:
Opt-in per-gash history, separate from the bounded online force observer.
Reconstructs the same overlapping rectangular window-mean radial loads.
This is not instantaneous tooth force. Times seconds, forces N.

fields.name: radialAt
fields.doc: Right-continuous radial window load for a later wall-source sweep.

types.name: HobbingForceSample
types.doc:
One gash's window-AVERAGE loads, not an instantaneous tooth peak.
mm³/mm²/mm inputs; N, Nm, W, J outputs. Table torque is a magnitude bound
(resultant force at work radius), not a signed force-vector prediction.

types.name: HobbingForces
types.doc:
Optional per-pass observer. A COW previous stock plus native interval comparison
gives removed volume, without copying circle intervals into the managed heap.
Call after EVERY pass in cutting order; unrelated stock edits invalidate attribution.
Summary storage is bounded. Pass means are rectangular loads over their windows;
maxima sum overlapping windows at each start. These are NOT tooth-force peaks.

fields.name: new
fields.doc:
edgeWidth is an explicitly assumed effective engaged cutting-edge width, mm;
interval volume alone cannot identify chip width and thickness separately.

types.name: HobbingKeyframe
types.doc: Controller sample. Rotary positions are unwrapped radians.

types.name: HobbingMotion
types.doc:
Linear interpolation of measured/controller axis samples, without coupling C
rigidly to B. Gash events can therefore use measured master phase while C keeps
its independent actual following error.

fields.name: timeAtMaster
fields.doc:
Monotone measured master; extrapolation only locates the centres of partial
engagement windows outside the run, never poses outside sampled time.

types.name: HobbingPoseOffset
types.doc:
Rigid translations in mm and work-table tilts in radians. Work offsets rotate with C; tool offsets
rotate with B. Separate frames prevent radial hob error becoming an X-only wobble.

types.name: HobbingReport
types.doc: Numerical convergence is observed on the sampled circles, not a machine accuracy grade.

types.name: HobbingStream
types.doc:
Bounded measured-motion window. Finishes each complete gash window exactly once,
retaining the bracketing controller samples until all overlapping windows are cut.

types.name: HobbingSweep
types.doc:
Sweeps the actual planar rake regions through sampled rigid poses. A native
convex-prism sweep supplies circle intervals; no target GearSpec or quality
formula is passed to the cutter. The sampler must resolve motion between its
time knots; maxTimeStep also caps sampling of nonlinear/perturbed trajectories.

fields.name: cut
fields.doc:
Transactional job. Refine the whole swept path until per-circle angular
symmetric differences, expressed as arc lengths, meet tolerance. On failure
the incoming stock is restored. Sources identify the exact scheduled pass.

fields.name: cutMany
fields.doc:
Converged inspection domains: retain every sampled circle, share poses,
and require the same arc-change bound on every domain at each refinement.

fields.name: cutPass
fields.doc:
One resolution, useful for convergence studies. Sampling still evaluates
true motion, including the exact pass-centre time between control ticks.

fields.name: cutPassMany
fields.doc: Identical poses for independent sampled stock domains.

types.name: IdealHobbingJob
types.doc:
External spur-gear driver, no machine/runtime coupling or error sources.
Reference rack module/pressure angle must match; positive feed advances +Z.

types.name: InspectionRingStock
types.doc:
Physical rake stock only at the circles read by GearMeasurement: all radial
samples at profile/pitch Z, all axial samples bracketing measurement radius.
Circle subtraction is independent; no uncut circle or target boundary is
supplied to inspection. Every retained coordinate must be bit-identical to
the dense grid. Unsupported coordinates fail rather than fabricate coverage.
Not a volume, load, mesh or force-feedback stock representation.

types.name: KienzleMaterial
types.doc:
Empirical coefficients, NOT a hardness/material database. kc11 is N/mm² at
h=1 mm, mc dimensionless. No rake, speed, wear or ploughing correction.

types.name: RingCompliance
types.doc:
Quasistatic in-plane n=2 thin-ring model. mm, N, Young's modulus N/mm².
w=d*cos(2 theta), U=9*pi*E*I*d²/(2R³), I=width*wall³/12.
Mandrel support is a separately stated generalized stiffness in parallel.
Higher modes, local tooth bending, contact lift-off and dynamics are omitted.
